artifact.self_contained_problem:
In perturbative QCD, the running strong coupling $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ is governed by the renormalization-group equation
$$Q^2\,\frac{d\alpha_s(Q^2)}{dQ^2} = \beta(\alpha_s) = -\alpha_s^2\bigl(b_0 + b_1\alpha_s + b_2\alpha_s^2 + b_3\alpha_s^3 + \cdots\bigr),$$
where the first two coefficients $b_0$ and $b_1$ are universal but the coefficients $b_i$ for $i\ge 2$ depend on the chosen renormalization scheme. A typical observable used to extract $\alpha_s$ at a momentum scale $Q$ has a perturbative expansion of the form
$$\delta_{\rm QCD}(Q) = \sum_{n\ge 1} c_n\,\alpha_s^n(Q^2),$$
where the coefficients $c_n$ are conjectured to grow factorially, $c_n \sim n!\,K^n$, due to renormalon singularities in the Borel plane that reflect non-perturbative power corrections of order $(\Lambda_{\rm QCD}^2/Q^2)^p$. As a result, the series is divergent (asymptotic), and truncations carry an irreducible ambiguity of size $\sim e^{-1/(b_0\alpha_s)}$.

Problem. Devise a determination of $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ from physical observables that simultaneously
(i) eliminates or controls the scheme dependence introduced by the higher beta-function coefficients $b_i$, $i\ge 2$, and
(ii) tames the factorial $n!\,\alpha_s^n$ renormalon-driven divergence of $\delta_{\rm QCD}(Q)$ — for instance by an unambiguous prescription that subtracts renormalon contributions while consistently incorporating the associated non-perturbative power corrections — so as to yield a value of $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ whose theoretical uncertainty can in principle be reduced below the present perturbative ambiguity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of achieving high-precision, scheme-independent determinations of $\alpha_s$ in the presence of renormalon-induced factorial divergences remains an active research area. Recent work (e.g., gradient-flow renormalon subtraction, R-improved static-energy determinations, renormalon-free gluon condensate schemes, and the Principle of Maximum Conformality) provides partial mitigation strategies but no universally accepted solution; scheme and perturbative-scale choices continue to materially affect extracted values.

status_evidence.title: A Precise α_s Determination from the R-improved QCD Static Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Recent determinations using R-improvement and renormalon subtraction in the static energy.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work attempts renormalon-subtracted high-precision α_s determinations, indicating the underlying problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Determination of α_s from static QCD potential: OPE with renormalon subtraction and lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: OPE with renormalon subtraction combined with lattice QCD to extract α_s.
status_evidence.claim: Renormalon subtraction is still being developed as a means of improving α_s extractions.

status_evidence.title: Renormalons (Beneke)
status_evidence.snippet: Review establishing factorial growth c_n ~ n! and the resulting irreducible perturbative ambiguity.
status_evidence.claim: The factorial divergence and associated ambiguity are intrinsic, motivating the open precision problem.

status_evidence.title: Gradient-flow renormalon subtraction and the hadronic tau decay series
status_evidence.snippet: Gradient flow used to define renormalon-free schemes for OPE.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing renormalon-subtraction frameworks indicate no canonical resolution yet.
